body:
**Good morning, Bakersfield.** It's Saturday, August 22, 2026, and we're starting the day with a high of 103° and air quality at moderate (AQI 74). Our top story this morning is the arrest of a 15-year-old suspect in connection with last night's deadly shooting at Independence High School's football game. Overnight, our crews handled a shooting outside a Taco Bell in east Bakersfield, a fire at a vacant house on King Street, and a two-vehicle collision with one car on fire at Gosford and Harris. Let's get you caught up.

## The Kern Overnight

The night's most serious call came just after midnight when a witness reported seeing someone shot at a Taco Bell in the Baker Street area. The suspect was described as a white male in his 40s to 50s wearing a black shirt and dark pants, sitting inside a white vehicle — possibly a Ford Explorer. Officers responded with an officer-safety broadcast. Before that, around 2:16 a.m., flames were visible inside a vacant single-story house on King Street with heavy smoke showing. Multiple engines and a truck company responded, and the fire was under control by about 2:25. Just before 11 p.m., a two-vehicle collision left one vehicle on fire near Gosford Road and Harris Road. Engine 14 and Engine 9 responded — one car was smoking with another about a quarter mile back — and command dubbed it the Harris Incident. Injuries were unknown. Multiple reports of a grass fire drew a large response — engines, patrol units, a water tender, a dozer and a helicopter — to southbound Highway 395 north of Brown Road. Crews found a small roadside fire that was quickly extinguished, and the extra equipment was canceled. Around 10:38 p.m., an assault with a knife was reported with no injuries. The suspect — about 6 feet tall with neck tattoos, wearing black shorts, a gray shirt and white shoes — fled on foot northbound. Other incidents included a subject reported with a firearm in his waistband on Houchin Road; an assault reported on Birch Avenue in Wasco; a hit-and-run on Monterey Street involving a black Camry and a white sedan; two fire hydrants spilling water on 22nd Street between Q and P streets; about a half acre burning behind a residence on Windsong Street; a suspicious vehicle check on Culiacan Avenue; a family disturbance on Suncrest Drive involving an intoxicated teenager; a welfare check on a man lying on the ground near the curb on 26th Street; and an assault in progress with multiple people inside and a disturbance heard.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 103° and a low around 75° tonight. It's currently 97° at Meadows Field (KBFL). No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County. Air quality is moderate at an AQI of 74. We're keeping an eye on conditions, but for now, it's a typical August day in the valley.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that** Bakersfield Mayor Karen Goh has released a statement addressing last night's deadly shooting at Independence High School. The mayor expressed her condolences to the victim's family and the community, emphasizing that public safety is a top priority. She urged anyone with information to come forward and cooperate with the ongoing investigation.

**According to 23ABC,** officials have announced the arrest of a 15-year-old suspect in connection with the deadly shooting at Independence High School's football game. The arrest was made Saturday morning in the 7500 block of Stockdale Highway. The investigation is ongoing, and no other suspects have been identified at this time.

**Bakersfield Now tells us that** Southwest Market has canceled its Saturday event at Independence High School following the fatal shooting. The decision was made out of respect for the victim's family and the community. Organizers expressed their condolences and announced that the event will be rescheduled.

## Something good

**Bakersfield Now shares** a heartwarming story about a local family hosting a flea market to raise $8,900 for Villafana's prosthetic leg. The event aims to support Villafana in obtaining the necessary medical device, and the community is encouraged to come out and show their support.

## Coming up this week

This week brings a variety of events and meetings to Bakersfield. On Tuesday, August 26, the City Council will hold a Special City Council Meeting at 12:00 p.m., followed by City Council Meeting 330 at 3:30 p.m. and City Council Meeting 515 at 5:15 p.m. For entertainment, the Fox Theater has a packed schedule: Los Yonic's Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio will perform on Saturday, August 22. On Tuesday, August 24, you can catch Cults & Classics: Season Pass 2026-2027. Rodney Carrington takes the stage on Thursday, August 27, followed by CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE on Friday, August 28. On Saturday, August 29, enjoy performances by Willie Barcena and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix. Be sure to check the Fox Theater's website for tickets and more information.
